item.title: Welcome to the PATH: Isolating Legacy Perl to Reduce Cognitive Load
item.description: On February 27, 2026, I had a meeting with my team lead, Pascal. The invite simply said “Discussion Marine <> Pascal”. I wondered if I had done something wrong. That is why my first reaction to his question was relief. He asked, “Do you want to work with the Perl legacy code full time?” Then came the surprise. Honestly, that was not the first thing that would come to mind when I was thinking about my full-time start. I had just graduated from a dual apprenticeship/university program. I thought I would spend the following years programming in our recent tech stack, namely Vue.js/TypeScript for the frontend and Elixir in the backend, having to touch our legacy Perl code only occasionally.

item.title: How to Start a Blog (in a Weekend)
item.description: I started my blog for three reasons: to show my work and document my progress, to build authority in my field, and because writing is way easier than creating videos or podcasts.
